The likely fault area is [qtargs.py](/app/qutebrowser/config/qtargs.py:56): it recognizes and merges `--enable-features=` but has no corresponding handling or prefix constant for `--disable-features=`. Values supplied through `--qt-flag` or `qt.args` already appear to remain in the constructed argument array unchanged, so the reported failure cannot be confirmed at this layer alone. A bare `--disable-features=...` command line option is not accepted by the parser.

The fix should verify both input routes with comma-separated enable and disable values, one merged enable entry, and each disable flag preserved separately. Existing tests cover only enable flags; all 82 Qt argument tests pass. I recorded the diagnosis in [checkpoint.md](/app/.codex-role-output/checkpoint.md). Under the assigned fault-localization scope, I did not edit project source or tests.

Updated [qtargs.py](/app/qutebrowser/config/qtargs.py) to recognize both feature flag prefixes. It now merges enabled features into one `--enable-features=` argument and preserves each `--disable-features=` argument separately, whether supplied through `--qt-flag` or `qt.args`.

Added mixed-source coverage in [test_qtargs.py](/app/tests/unit/config/test_qtargs.py). All 84 Qt argument tests pass; `git diff --check` is clean.

VERDICT: ACCEPT

The patch meets the stated QtWebEngine argument requirements. It merges enabled features into one flag, preserves each disable flag as a separate, unmodified argument, and handles flags from both command line and configuration. I found no code defect.

`python -m pytest -q tests/unit/config/test_qtargs.py` — **84 passed**. `git diff --check` — **passed**. No test environment problem.
